newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Brazil completes federal rail privatization.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brazil completes federal rail privatization.

text.p: Brazil completed the privatization of its federal railway network on Friday by auctioning off a 30-year concession to operate the Northeast section for 15.8 million reais ($14.6 million).
The price, about 38 percent more than the minimum set for the concession, brought the total amount raised by privatizing six railway sections to 1.99 billion reais ($1.84 billion).
"This is a very positive result," Transport Minister Eliseu Padilha told reporters after the auction, held at the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange.

The winning consortium is composed of four Brazilian companies: the Vicunha group; steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Nacional SA, or CSN ; Companhia Vale do Rio Doce SA , the recently privatized mining concern known as CVRD; and Banco Bradesco SA. Vicunha has a 40 percent stake in the consortium, while the others have 20 percent each.
The 2,924.4-mile (4,679 km) Northeast railway links the states of Maranhao, Piaui, Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Alagoas and Sergipe.

It is also connected with CVRD's company railway, which runs from the Amazon mining enclave of Carajas to the port of Sao Luis in Maranhao state. It extends to the former Center-East rail section, now known as Ferrovia Centro Atlantica.

Mozart Litwinski, CSN's superintendant for infrastructure, said the consortium planned to invest at least 36 million reais in the railway over the next five years and possibly as much as 100 million reais ($92.6 million) over the next 10 years, depending on demand.
"With these investment levels, the capacity of the railway could double," he said.

The federal railway network is already investing $60 million to upgrade the Northeast section, which was in poor condition. The money is coming from a World Bank loan of $350 million aimed at preparing the network for privatization.
The Northeast rail section currently carries total freight volume of 785 million tonnes per kilometer.

The president of the federal railway network, Isaac Popoutchi, has said volume could quickly rise to 1.2 billion tonnes per kilometer and to 1.8 billion tonnes in six years. He cited estimates that the market's potential was 2.2 billion tonnes per kilometer. The railway carries mainly fuel, cement and agricultural products.

"The Northeast (of Brazil) is today a major source of opportunities with fantastic growth rates," he said. "It is a very well structured railway and with the necessary investment it can develop its potential."
The new operators have until July 25 to pay the first installment of 6.63 million reais ($6.1 million) and the remaining amount in 109 installments over three years.

The only Brazilian railway that remains to be privatized is Sao Paulo state's Fepasa. An operating concession is expected to be auctioned by the end of the year, according to Jose Pio Borges, the vice president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which oversees the country's privatization program.
